title: The Current of the Sepik Basin
premise: Paloma Thackeray, a salvage diver scraping a living from the Sepik River's drowned wrecks, recovers a sealed chest bearing the long-extinct seal of a colonial trading nation — inside it, a ledger mapping a wartime cache that three desperate parties want: a corrupt naval officer, a mercenary crew, and the descendants of the village that hid it. When her boat is burned and her mentor killed, Paloma flees upriver with Elias Wari, a quiet cartographer whose family name appears in the ledger, and together they navigate monsoon floods, betrayals, and the river's own memory of what was buried. In the drowned grotto at the basin's heart, Paloma must choose between selling the cache to buy her freedom and returning it to the village that never stopped waiting for it. She chooses belonging over escape, and the river keeps its secret — and her.
about_author: Kestrel Lockridge is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent six years charting waterways across Papua New Guinea and Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. Their novels blend hard-edged adventure with an anthropologist's patience for the places where rivers remember more than people do.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Diving a navy-restricted wreck on the Sepik, Paloma salvages scrap and keeps her head down, haunted by the brother she lost to this same river. She surfaces with a rusted chest stamped with a dead nation's seal. The beat is restless competence masking grief; the discovery cracks open the life she's carefully contained.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Captain Voss
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. In her stilt-house workshop she pries the chest open: a captain's ledger mapping a wartime cache and naming local families who sheltered it — including 'Wari.' A naval officer, Commander Reyes, arrives asking questions he shouldn't know to ask. Beat: dread blooming under curiosity as Paloma realizes the chest marks her.

chapters.title: Fire on the Stilt-House
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Mercenaries torch her home in the night; her old mentor Tio dies covering her escape. She flees downriver in her leaking dive boat with the ledger and nothing else. Beat: raw loss and survivor's guilt; the wilderness that forgives nothing now has a debt against her name.

chapters.title: The Cartographer at Angoram
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Elias Wari, a government mapmaker estranged from his village, recognizes his family name when Paloma begs passage and supplies. He agrees to guide her upriver — partly for the truth about his grandfather's role in hiding the cache. Beat: wary alliance between two people who both fled their own histories.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The rains break early. Racing flooded channels with Reyes's patrol boat behind them, they lose their fuel cache and shelter in a drowned mission church. Paloma teaches Elias salvage diving; he teaches her to read the river's moods. Beat: found family taking root in shared danger and small kindnesses.

chapters.title: The Village That Waited
chapters.summary: POV Elias. They reach Elias's home village, where elders confirm the ledger's story: his grandfather helped hide the cache to keep it from being looted, then carried the shame of silence to his grave. Some villagers want it returned; one cousin has already sold information to the mercenaries. Beat: belonging offered — and complicated by betrayal.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Confluence
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The mercenaries strike at dawn where two rivers meet. Paloma scuttles her own boat to block the channel, saving the villagers but destroying her last means of escape. Captured briefly by Reyes, she learns the navy wants the cache buried again — along with everyone who's seen the ledger. Beat: sacrifice; escape redefined as something worth less than people.

chapters.title: The Grotto of the Dead Nation
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Guided by the ledger's final cipher and the elders' songs, Elias and Paloma find the sea-cave grotto behind a waterfall: crates of looted art, gold, and records of atrocities the dead empire erased. Reyes arrives with the mercenaries, and the monsoon flood begins swallowing the cave. Beat: awe curdling into siege; the past literally closing in.

chapters.title: The River Takes Its Due
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Climax. In rising water, Paloma turns the grotto's own collapse into a weapon, drowning the mercenaries' advantage while Elias carries the evidence out to the elders. Reyes, refusing retreat, is taken by the flood he tried to command. Beat: fury transmuted into resolve; memory winning over erasure at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Aftermath: the village claims the returned heritage, the navy's cover quietly collapses, and Paloma — offered passage anywhere — stays to help raise the stilt-house where Tio's tools hang drying. Elias begins drawing new maps, with her name in the margins. Beat: grief settled into gratitude; the river forgets nothing, and neither will she — but now she remembers among family.
